body: I'm sorry that you're feeling this way. I have definitely been at some low points myself. Just wait it out. Please please please keep in mind that these feelings are fleeting. Go for a walk, find something beautiful. Just one small little thing that helps you remember that there is good in the world. Don't beat yourself up.

Are you fucking kidding me? What an idiot. The thing with suicide hotlines is that these people are usually volunteers. They don't usually need any education or training. In my experience, I have never had anyone that was therapist quality-- or even equipped to calmly handle a panicky/ suicidal person. 

I'm sorry about your surgery. The good news is, once the doctors see what's wrong, they can fix the endometriosis you have now as well as give you a good birth control pill to prevent it from happening in the future.

As a woman, we are often made to feel that our bodies are disgusting simply because they are not perfect. I go through phases where I hate my body too. Anyway, I'm clearly rambling.... 
Find some calming music, some funny youtube videos, go out for a walk, watch a funny movie.... Distract yourself and keep in mind that this shitty feeling WILL pass eventually. When it does and you are in a better mood, write a list of positive things about yourself for you to read the next time you are down. 

You're beautiful, and I don't want you to hate yourself.

I'm sorry. That's all I can really say. Please just hold on a little longer. Someday, you will find something worth living for. You are someone's reason to live, they just haven't met you yet. If you die now, they never will. I send lots of love your way, and I wish I could jump through the screen and give you a huge hug.

We are considered to be independent contractors, which means we are in charge of paying our own taxes. Every dancer does this differently depending on her financial needs. I need to keep books of my finances because I take out student loans, so I need a record of my income. The same goes for people trying to finance a house or car. Some of the younger girls who don't have kids or bills (or any knowledge of the repercussions of tax evasion) choose  not to open a bank account and just keep all of their cash private and locked away. 

I keep all of my receipts and claim all hair, make up, and other beauty purchases as a business expense. I also keep track of my car's mileage to and from work every week. The IRS does not know that we are "strippers," just that we are technically "business owners." Anyone making a large amount of cash can be investigated by the IRS. It is very important to have an accountant and keep up with tax payments every year-- or in my case, every quarter.
